note:
Round 2 of the /pages/contact banner. Malcolm chose three frames from the first wave and then corrected the register: 'we should be using the graphite branding style background. See other page banners.'

HE IS RIGHT AND ROUND 1 WAS OFF-BRAND. Pulling the six live page banners down and looking at them together makes it obvious: acetyl, copper-peptide, PDRN, the-science and skin-concerns are all a deep graphite sweep at #1A1A1A falling to near-black, subject hard-lit on the RIGHT, empty unlit graphite on the LEFT carrying the headline. Round 1 came back high-key - bright white clinic, soft north window, pale walls - which is the opposite register and would have sat on the site as the one banner that did not belong.

skin-concerns is the precedent that matters here, because it is the one with a PERSON on graphite: low-key, a single hard key, strong falloff, dark ground running to the edges. Not a bright room dimmed - lit dark from the start.

TWO READINGS OF THE BRIEF, AND THIS WAVE COVERS BOTH. 'These are the best, but use the graphite background' can mean (a) keep these exact frames and restyle the ground, or (b) re-shoot these compositions in the graphite register. They give different faces, so guessing would be wrong half the time.

  - CLASS B slots (-fresh) regenerate the composition text-to-image, correctly lit for graphite from the start. New faces, integrated lighting.
  - CLASS A slots (-restyle) send Malcolm's chosen frame as a reference so the people survive. ⚠️ Expect these to be the weaker half: relighting a high-key photograph to low-key is exactly where an edit pass leaves the subject lit for the OLD ground and the result reads as a composite. Judge the light direction on the face against the ground, not the likeness.

The three compositions, described from Malcolm's actual picks so the fresh slots do not drift:
  D-seated-wider-gpt_image_01 - client left of pair (warm brown skin, long dark wavy hair, oatmeal V-neck) looking up at clinician right (fair, dark hair in a low ponytail, white coat over white top)
  B-two-faces-gpt_image_02   - clinician centre-right (warm olive, dark chin-length bob, white coat over pale blue collarless top) speaking to client right (fair, loose silver-grey hair, grey knit)
  A-speaking-flux2_01        - clinician centre-right (warm olive, dark hair drawn back, white coat over grey top) smiling at a client who is only the back of a head at the right edge

THE COAT IS THE NEW RISK. White cotton against near-black clips to paper-white and loses the lapel, which is how a coat stops reading as a coat. Every slot says it holds detail in the key light and falls into deep shadow on its unlit side, and 'blown out' / 'clipped white' are negated.

The left 45 percent is stated as LIT GRAPHITE GROUND with smooth continuous gradation and no visible edge, band or line - never as 'empty' or 'quiet'. Dark is wanted here, unlike the FAQ macro, but a hard-edged black band is still the failure mode.

⚠️ Luma is included per rule 1 but its output is NOT usable at this ratio: measured 2026-08-30, it snaps a 2.400:1 request to 2784x1504 = 1.851:1 on every slot. Look at it for composition, never for a shippable frame.

slots.title: D composition, graphite register, generated fresh
slots.prompt:
A photorealistic wide editorial photograph, 2.4:1 letterbox format, of a skin clinician and her client in conversation, lit low-key against a dark studio ground.

The pair occupy the right 55 percent of the frame. On the right, the clinician is a woman in her forties with fair skin and dark brown hair drawn back into a low ponytail, wearing a plain white cotton clinical coat over a plain white top. The coat is completely plain - no pocket badge, no embroidery, no printed characters of any kind. Her head and shoulders sit from about 0.72 to 0.94 of the frame width and from about 0.16 to 0.80 of the frame height, turned toward the client on her left, speaking with a warm, easy smile.

To her left the client is a woman in her early thirties with warm brown skin and long dark wavy hair, seen from about 0.50 to 0.72 of the frame width, her face lifted slightly toward the clinician, smiling and attentive. She wears a plain oatmeal V-neck knit. Her face is in sharp focus and is the brighter of the two.

LIGHT: one hard key light from the front-left at head height, modelling both faces with clear directional shaping and a defined shadow side, plus a single soft fill at low level so the shadows retain detail without lifting the scene. The falloff is strong - light drops away quickly behind them.

GROUND: a seamless deep graphite sweep, colour hex 1A1A1A, unlit behind the pair and falling off to near black toward the left edge and the top edge. The left 45 percent of the frame, measured from 0 to 0.45 of frame width, is that graphite ground held at an even low tone with smooth continuous gradation and no visible edge, band, line, stripe or vignette ring anywhere, so a headline can sit on it unaided. The ground reaches the top, bottom and left edges of the frame. There is nothing in it - no furniture, no window, no signage, no artwork, no object of any kind.

Both women show real, unretouched skin - visible pores, fine lines, faint natural colour variation - lit so texture is present without being emphasised. Neither face is smoothed.

The white coat holds its detail: it reads as white where the key light strikes it and falls into deep shadow on its unlit side, with the lapel, collar and seams still visible. It is never blown out to flat paper-white anywhere.

Colour is graphite, near-black, white and natural skin tones only. Shot on a full-frame camera with an 85mm lens at f/2.2, deep colour, natural, no filter, magazine-quality editorial photography.
slots.negative_extra: no hands in frame, no desk, no chair reading as a recognisable object

slots.title: D restyled from Malcolm's chosen frame, people preserved
slots.prompt:
Keep the two women in the reference photograph exactly as they are - the same faces, the same hair, the same clothing, the same poses, the same expressions and the same positions in the frame. Change only the environment and the lighting.

Replace the bright pale room behind them with a seamless deep graphite studio sweep, colour hex 1A1A1A, unlit behind them and falling off to near black toward the left edge and the top edge. The left 45 percent of the frame, measured from 0 to 0.45 of frame width, becomes that graphite ground held at an even low tone with smooth continuous gradation and no visible edge, band, line, stripe or vignette ring anywhere. Nothing remains in the background - no furniture, no window, no wall detail, no object of any kind. The ground reaches the top, bottom and left edges.

Relight both women to match that ground: one hard key light from the front-left at head height giving each face clear directional modelling and a defined shadow side, plus a single soft fill at low level. The light must fall away quickly behind them so they sit in the dark rather than in front of it. Their shadow sides must genuinely darken - do not keep the flat, evenly lit look of the reference.

The white coat holds its detail: white where the key light strikes it, falling into deep shadow on its unlit side, lapel and collar still readable, never blown out to flat paper-white.

Skin stays real and unretouched - visible pores, fine lines, faint natural colour variation. Do not smooth either face. Colour is graphite, near-black, white and natural skin tones only. Photorealistic editorial photography, deep colour, no filter.
slots.negative_extra: no change to either face, no change of pose, no bright rim light outlining the subjects, no cut-out composite edge
